title: npx, Yarn PnP, and Execution Models
description: Run package binaries without installing them, and understand node_modules versus Plug'n'Play versus pnpm's store.

data.text: Not every tool deserves a place in `package.json`. Runners such as `npx` and `yarn dlx` execute a package without adding it to your dependencies, and **execution models** decide whether your packages live in `node_modules` at all.

data.title: One-off tools with npx, Yarn dlx, and pnpm dlx
data.code:
npx create-next-app@latest my-app
npx --yes prettier@3 --write .

# Yarn Berry
yarn dlx create-next-app@latest my-app

# pnpm
pnpm dlx create-next-app@latest my-app

data.text: `npx` first looks for the binary in `node_modules/.bin` (so it runs your locally installed, version-pinned tool), then the npm cache, and only downloads as a last resort. That is why `npm run` and `npx` agree on which version of `eslint` they run.

data.title: Unpinned npx is a supply-chain risk
data.text: `npx some-tool` runs whatever version is published right now. Always pin (`npx tool@1.2.3`) in documentation and CI, and prefer adding stable tools as devDependencies.

Yarn Berry can store packages in a global cache and generate a single `.pnp.cjs` file that maps every import to a zip path. Installs become faster, the tree is checked for undeclared dependencies, and CI can skip extraction entirely. The trade-off is tooling that assumes `node_modules` on disk.

data.caption: .yarnrc.yml — choose the linker
data.code:
nodeLinker: pnp        # default in Yarn 4 (no node_modules)
# or
nodeLinker: node-modules  # compatibility escape hatch

data.title: Adopt PnP and handle tools that need real files
data.code:
yarn install                     # writes .pnp.cjs + .yarn/cache
node .yarn/sdks/typescript/bin/tsc --noEmit

yarn add -D @yarnpkg/pnpify
yarn pnpify --sdk vscode         # editor discovers types

data.caption: Execution models: node_modules, PnP, and pnpm store
data.definition:
flowchart TD
    A[Import request] --> B{Linker}
    B -->|node_modules| C[Resolve file in node_modules]
    B -->|PnP| D[Resolve zip path via .pnp.cjs]
    B -->|pnpm| E[Resolve symlink into virtual store]
    C --> F[Load package]
    D --> F
    E --> F

terms.definition: Runners that execute a package binary without adding it to package.json.
A Yarn install strategy that removes node_modules and resolves imports from zipped packages in a global cache.
The Yarn setting that selects pnp or node-modules resolution.
Yarn Berry's zero-install cache of package zips, optionally committed for offline installs.

data.title: Key takeaways
points: npx and yarn dlx run binaries without polluting dependencies — pin versions.
PnP removes node_modules, speeds up installs, and rejects undeclared dependencies.
nodeLinker: node-modules is the pragmatic fallback when a tool needs real files.
pnpm keeps a content-addressable store and symlinks packages into place.
data.takeaway: Knowing the three node_modules strategies and their trade-offs is what separates "I use npm" from "I understand the toolchain".
